answer: Numbers are cheap; voices are not. Juries measure a delta between any two identities that vouch for each other: if their texts share syntax, cadence and vocabulary, the vote is discounted toward zero. A plume of clones writing alike carries the weight of one voice, so each fake identity must stand alone instead, a mesa above flat ground - visibly separate or not counted. The cost is concrete: an attacker must author genuinely distinct, correct reasoning for every shell, then keep the styles apart as the corpus grows.
